newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian PM backs closure of troubled bank.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian PM backs closure of troubled bank.

text.p: Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius on Thursday said the government would shut Innovation Bank, once one of the largest commercial banks in the Baltic state but which was declared insolvent in 1995.
Vagnorius said the price tag to liquidate the bank and repay depositors could reach 350 million litas.
The bank's closure at the end of 1995, followed by that of another leading bank, Litimpeks, sparked a serious bank crisis.
"Innovation will be liquidated. The government will take over its assets and the process will take only a few months," Vagnorius told a news conference.
Litimpeks has since been allowed to reopen and is now seeking a foreign investor to get it back into shape.
"The government will compensate private depositors up to 8,000 litas...4,000 litas in 1997 and the other 4,000 litas before the end of 1998," Vagnorius added.
"Deposits worth over 8,000 litas will be compensated through the issue of government treasury bills," he added.
The bank sector has recovered well after the crisis but many Lithuanians continue to view banks with deep suspicion.
